MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

1. Parties
Party A: Hanwool Living Co., Ltd.
Address: 00, Dosan-daero, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea
Representative: Managing Director, Motion Furniture Division
Contact: legal@hanwool-living.example

Party B: Beihai Motion Technology Co., Ltd.
Address: No. 00, Longgang District, Shenzhen, People's Republic of China
Representative: General Manager, Overseas Business Division
Contact: overseas@beihai-motion.example

Party A and Party B are collectively referred to as the "Parties" and individually as a "Party".

2. Purpose
1. The parties intend to engage in technical exchanges, business discussions, sample testing, solution evaluation, and
preliminary development cooperation concerning motion bed actuators, controllers, and related control software
(the "Project").
2. To protect the trade secrets, technical materials, product materials, development materials, and other confidential information
exchanged in the course of the Project, the parties enter into this Agreement.

3. Definitions
1. "Disclosing Party" means the party that discloses Confidential Information to the other party during the cooperation under this
Agreement.
2. "Receiving Party" means the party that receives, accesses, uses, or keeps the Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party
under this Agreement.
3. This Agreement imposes mutual confidentiality obligations on both parties. Unless the context clearly provides otherwise, the
obligations in this Agreement apply to both Parties equally.

4. Scope of Confidential Information
1. "Confidential Information" under this Agreement means all information disclosed by one party to the other party in any form,
whether in writing, orally, electronically, or by demonstration of samples, in connection with the Project.
2. Confidential Information includes, but is not limited to, drawings, know-how, technical solutions, processes, charts, designs,
circuit diagrams, firmware, source code, control logic, test data, quality data, cost information, supplier information, customer
information, business plans, and price conditions.
3. Confidential Information also includes experience accumulation, technical judgment logic, testing methods, debugging methods,
and failure analysis methods that are not generally known in the relevant industry.
4. Information not marked as confidential shall be treated as Confidential Information only where, by its nature or the
circumstances of disclosure, a reasonable person would understand it to be confidential.

5. Confidentiality Obligations
1. The Receiving Party undertakes to use the Confidential Information solely for the cooperation purpose set forth in Section 2 of
this Agreement.
2. Except as expressly permitted under this Agreement, the Receiving Party shall not disclose, transfer, or provide the Disclosing
Party's Confidential Information to any third party.
3. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information, on a need-to-know basis and to the extent necessary for the Project,
to its officers, employees, affiliates, advisers, and third-party development, testing, or certification companies that are bound by
confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Agreement, provided that for core technical information designated in
writing by the Disclosing Party the Receiving Party shall obtain the Disclosing Party's prior written consent before any such
disclosure.
4. The Receiving Party shall take reasonable protective measures no less stringent than those used to protect its own similar
confidential information, and in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.
5. The Receiving Party shall not use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to infringe the Disclosing Party's intellectual
property rights; independent development by the Receiving Party without use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information,
including cooperation with third parties without use of such Confidential Information, shall not be restricted by this Agreement.

6. Special Protection for Party B SDK, API and Protocol
1. If Party B provides any SDK, API, Protocol, interface protocol, sample code, development document, or other technical material
to Party A for the Project, such material constitutes a specially protected technical asset of Party B and requires the prior
written consent of Party B for any use beyond the Project.
2. Without Party B's prior written consent, Party A and its affiliates, employees, partners, or third-party development companies
shall not decompile, disassemble, or reverse engineer such material.
3. Without Party B's prior written consent, Party A shall not delete, modify, circumvent, or bypass any technical protection
measure applied to such material.
4. Party A shall not resell, assign, lease, or lend any SDK, API, Protocol, sample code, development document, or related material.
5. Party A shall not use the SDK, API, Protocol, or related materials provided by Party B to develop, improve, or perfect any
competing actuator or controller product.
6. Party A shall not copy, disseminate, or upload Party B's technical materials to any public network, code platform, sharing
service, or generative AI service.

7. Third-Party Development and Joint Development
1. Party A may engage Korean development companies or other third parties for APP, server, algorithm, interface, system
integration, and certification work in connection with the Project, provided that where such engagement requires access to core
technical information of Party B, Party A shall obtain Party B's prior written consent.
2. Party A shall notify Party B in writing in advance of the identity, scope of work, and scope of access of any third party that will
access Party B's Confidential Information.
3. Party A shall be responsible for the acts of any third-party development company, advisor, or partner designated or engaged by
Party A as if they were the acts of Party A.
4. Each party retains ownership of the technology, know-how, software, algorithms, data, and intellectual property it owned before
the date of this Agreement or developed independently outside the Project, and nothing in this Agreement transfers such
ownership to the other party.

8. Use, Copying, and Management of Materials
1. The Receiving Party may copy Confidential Information only to the extent necessary for the performance of this project. All
copies remain the property of the Disclosing Party.
2. The Receiving Party shall establish a reasonable information access authorization management system and restrict access to
those personnel who require the Confidential Information for the Project.
3. The Receiving Party shall not upload Confidential Information to any public code repository, public collaboration platform, or
external generative AI service.
4. If the Receiving Party discovers any leakage, loss, unauthorized access, or risk of leakage of Confidential Information, it shall
notify the Disclosing Party in writing without undue delay.

9. Intellectual Property and Ownership
1. Disclosure of Confidential Information by the Disclosing Party shall not be deemed to transfer, license, or grant to the Receiving
Party any right in such Confidential Information.
2. Each party retains ownership of the technology, materials, drawings, code, SDK, API, Protocol, software, algorithms, data, and
intellectual property that it owned before this Agreement or that it developed independently, and no license is granted by
implication.
3. Ownership of any development results, deliverables, improvements, modifications, derivative technology, or interface adaptation
created in the course of the Project shall be determined by a separate development agreement or other separate written agreement
to be concluded between the parties, and shall not be determined by this Agreement.
4. This Agreement does not create any purchase, development, exclusive cooperation, or mass-production obligation. Each party
remains free to conduct its own research, development, and business activities.

10. Exceptions to Confidential Information
1. The following information shall not be subject to the confidentiality obligations under this Agreement, provided that the
Receiving Party bears the burden of proof:
2. Information that was already publicly known at the time of disclosure;
3. Information that becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party;
4. Information that the Receiving Party legally possessed without confidentiality obligations before disclosure by the Disclosing
Party;
5. Information lawfully obtained by the Receiving Party from a third party who has the right to disclose such information;
6. Information independently developed by the Receiving Party without using the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information;
7. Information that must be disclosed pursuant to the requirements of law, court, governmental authority, or regulatory body.

11. Return and Destruction of Materials
1. If the cooperation is terminated, the project is canceled, the Disclosing Party makes a written request, or this Agreement is
terminated, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy the Confidential Information in its possession.
2. For information that cannot be immediately destroyed due to system backups, compliance retention, or legal requirements, the
Receiving Party may retain such information for the minimum period required, and the confidentiality obligations under this
Agreement shall continue to apply to the retained information during that period.
3. The Disclosing Party has the right to request a written destruction confirmation from the Receiving Party.

12. Term of Confidentiality
1. This Agreement shall become effective as of the date of signature by both parties.
2. The confidentiality obligations for general Confidential Information shall remain in effect for five (5) years from the date each
item of Confidential Information is disclosed.
3. For information qualifying as a trade secret under applicable law, the confidentiality obligations shall continue for as long as the
information retains its status as a trade secret.
4. Even if the cooperation relationship, business contract, development contract, or this Agreement is terminated, the Receiving
Party shall continue to perform the obligations that by their nature survive termination.

13. Liability for Breach
1. If the Receiving Party breaches this Agreement and causes the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to be leaked,
misappropriated, or used beyond the permitted scope, the Receiving Party shall compensate the Disclosing Party for the resulting
damage.
2. Recoverable damages shall be limited to direct damages that have a proximate causal relationship to the breach and are
reasonably foreseeable, and indirect, special, incidental, and consequential damages shall be excluded.
3. If the Receiving Party's breach may cause irreparable harm to the Disclosing Party, the Disclosing Party has the right to require
the Receiving Party to cease the breach and to seek injunctive relief.
4. If the Receiving Party breaches this Agreement, the Disclosing Party has the right to suspend or terminate relevant technical
cooperation and the supply of materials.

14. Data Security and Personal Information
1. If user data, sleep data, health-related data, APP user information, server data, or other personal information is involved during
the Project, both parties shall comply with the applicable laws of the Republic of Korea and the People's Republic of China
concerning the protection of personal information.
2. Without authorization from the data subject and written confirmation by both parties, neither party shall arbitrarily collect, use,
transfer, or provide such data to any third party.
3. The parties shall enter into a separate written technical agreement or data processing agreement regarding server construction,
data storage location, cross-border transfer, and the allocation of roles between controller and processor before any personal
information is actually processed.

15. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
1. The formation, validity, interpretation, and performance of this Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the Republic of
Korea, without regard to its conflict of laws rules.
2. Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall first be resolved through good-faith consultation. If not
resolved within thirty (30) days, the dispute shall be finally settled by arbitration in Seoul under the rules of the Korean
Commercial Arbitration Board, and the arbitral award shall be final and binding on both parties.
3. During the dispute resolution period, except for the matters in dispute, the parties shall continue to perform their obligations
under this Agreement.

16. Miscellaneous
1. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties regarding confidentiality matters and supersedes any
prior understanding on the same subject.
2. Any amendment, supplement, or change to this Agreement shall become effective only after it is signed in writing by the
authorized representatives of both parties.
3. If any provision of this Agreement is deemed invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the validity of the remaining provisions shall not
be affected.
4. This Agreement shall be prepared and signed in three versions: Chinese, English, and Korean.
5. If there is any unclear, ambiguous, or conflicting wording or meaning among the Chinese, English, and Korean versions, the
English version shall prevail for the purpose of interpretation.
6. This Agreement is executed in two counterparts, with each party holding one counterpart, and each counterpart shall have the
same legal effect.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date last written below.

Party A: Hanwool Living Co., Ltd.          Party B: Beihai Motion Technology Co., Ltd.
Signature: ______________________          Signature: ______________________
Date: ______________________               Date: ______________________
